instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires principals (not lobbyists) to file periodic expense statements and requires lobbyists only to provide information to the principal, indicating no standalone lobbyist spending report filing requirement.
Section 13.68 sets a semiannual filing cadence for principals’ expense statements but does not establish any cadence for a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.
The only periodic spending statement described is the principal’s, due July 31 and January 31, not annually and not by lobbyists.
No provision requires lobbyists to file monthly spending reports; the only periodic report in the text is the principal’s semiannual expense statement.
The statute specifies semiannual principal filings and contains no quarterly lobbyist spending report requirement.
Although principals file semiannually, the question concerns a lobbyist’s periodic spending report and the statute does not require lobbyists to file such a report at any cadence.
No triannual spending report filing is described for lobbyists.
The statute contains no alternative ('other') cadence for a lobbyist-filed spending report; lobbyists only supply information to principals.

Total lobbying expenditures are reported in the principal’s expense statement, while lobbyists are only required to provide supporting information to the principal, not file a report including totals.
Compensation to lobbyists is included in the principal’s aggregate totals, but there is no requirement for the lobbyist to file a periodic spending report disclosing total compensation.
The statute requires principals to list each lobbyist and total amounts paid when exceeding $200, but does not require lobbyists to file a payer-broken-down compensation report.
Lobbyists provide information to principals for principal filings and separately apply for licenses, but no lobbyist periodic spending report is required to include lobbyist contact information.
The periodic expense statement is filed by the principal, so the statute does not impose on lobbyists any requirement to file a report listing principal names.
Principal contact information is part of principal registration and principal expense statements, not a lobbyist-filed spending report.
Business activity/nature disclosures are required in the principal’s registration statement, not in any lobbyist spending report.
Identifiers for legislative proposals/rules/topics are reported by principals under §13.67 and time-per-topic by principals under §13.68, not by lobbyists in a periodic spending report.
Bill identifiers are part of the principal’s reporting obligations under §13.67, and the statute does not require lobbyists to file a spending report listing bill numbers.
Topics/issues must be reported by the principal to the commission, but no lobbyist periodic spending report is required to include general issues.
Reasonably specific topic/subject-matter descriptions are required of principals’ topic reports, not of any lobbyist-filed spending report.
Section 13.67 requires identifying proposals/topics but does not require a lobbyist or principal to report a position (support/oppose) in any lobbyist spending report.
Principals must report time spent meeting with officials and other lobbying activity, but there is no lobbyist periodic spending report requiring disclosure of contacts made.

The principal’s expense statement reports aggregate totals and time proportions for topics, but does not require a lobbyist to file or to break expenditures down per issue in a lobbyist spending report.
Expense categorization is prescribed for the principal’s expense statement, and the statute does not impose a lobbyist-filed report categorizing expenses by type.
The law largely prohibits furnishing lodging/transportation/food etc., and where reimbursement is authorized it is reported by the principal, not by lobbyists in a periodic spending report.
Office overhead/indirect costs are addressed in the principal’s expense statement requirements, not in a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.
The statute requires certain disclosures in the principal’s expense statement but does not require lobbyists to file an itemized expense report with the commission.
Daily itemization of time is required in the principal’s filing, but there is no requirement for lobbyists to submit an itemized-format spending report to the commission.
Because the statute does not require a lobbyist to file a periodic spending report at all, it also does not require a lobbyist to file one when there is no activity.

The only household-member reference concerns an exception to the gift/pecuniary value prohibition for relatives/household members of the lobbyist or principal, not a lobbyist spending report disclosure scope.
